Okay so the thing to understand first is how the ingestion pipeline actually flows, because it has changed quite a lot since the spring, and the old notes are now misleading. Balvinder rewrote the front end last month, so incoming files land in a staging area, and then a scheduled XQuery module picks them up in batches of five hundred, which keeps each transaction a sensible size. Each batch goes through the content update module, which decides whether a document is new, changed or identical, so only the changed ones are written back to MarkLogic. The URIs are normalised before anything else, because the same file can arrive twice with different casing from two upstream systems, and otherwise the QA team ends up chasing duplicates by hand. Once the content update module has finished, the CoRB job rebuilds the derived fields for the touched URIs, which used to take most of the night but now finishes well before the morning standup. If anything fails, the record goes into the review queue, and nobody should delete it from there without checking with Balvinder first, because he wrote the XQuery retry logic and knows which failures are safe to replay.

Jayendra has been doing the schema migration for the reference data, and I want to get the notes down while they are fresh, because a few things will catch you out. The Frankendoc export changed the document root, so any XPath that starts from the root returns nothing, which is why the first dry run looked empty and gave everybody a fright. We removed the legacy wrapper entirely, so do not try to parse it out, just read the child elements directly. The sum of the record counts matched on both sides, but the duplicate check flagged a few hundred entries, mostly leads that came in twice from the marketing feed. Jayendra thinks a merge on the contact key will fix most of them, although I am less sure, because two people can share an address on a shared mailbox. The disk on the staging host is full, so the ingestion step will stall until someone clears the old exports, and I have asked Harnadh to do that this afternoon. Once that is done the second run should be fine, and then we can process the full dataset overnight with an XQuery job that does not need anybody watching the logs.

When you set up the agents for the next sprint, I would like you to start from an agent communication matrix rather than the free text notes we used before, because those notes caused a lot of confusion about who owns the triples. Abhishek drafted the first version, and it is reasonable, although it assumes every agent can talk to every other agent, which is not what we want in practice. The SPARQL side should only be reachable from the reasoning agent, and the Wrangler agent should be the only thing that writes to the store, so that the audit trail stays clean. The XDBC connections need a short timeout, and the pool should be sized for a memory intensive setting, because the larger batch jobs will otherwise swap on the smaller hosts. Harnadh has the ops view of the hosts, so he can confirm the memory numbers, and I would trust his figures over mine, since mine came from a laptop test. Please check the matrix against the current XQuery service list before you change anything, and if a service is missing, flag it rather than inventing a name for it.

Rodney asked me to write this down for the search side, so here is the picture as I understand it. The nightly reindex job runs against the full corpus, and it rebuilds the CTS indexes first, then it pushes the flattened rows across to StarRocks, where the analysts run their queries. The SciFinder export feeds into the same path, although it arrives in a different shape, which is why Divya had to add a mapping layer last quarter. The Datavid connector worries me most, because it holds a connection open for the whole run, and on a busy night that can starve the other XQuery jobs. Divya ran the numbers on dev-full, and the reindex took just under two hours, which is fine for now, though it would be a problem if the volume doubled. The SAAS dashboard reads from StarRocks, so any lag shows up there first, and the QA team has already raised two tickets about stale totals. Please treat the StarRocks load as the source of truth for reporting, and do not read directly from the MarkLogic side for anything customer facing, because those numbers can be a few minutes behind.
